reflection_diagnosis.causal_diagnosis: The policy under iter_006 achieves 40% success-like terminal rate (up from 20% in iter_001) and 0% timeout (down from 80%), but 60% unsafe terminal rate. The dominant component by absolute return is crash_penalty (-50.0), with dominance_ratio 4.53 and dense_to_objective_ratio 16.94. The success_bonus (100) is never triggered (mean 0.0) because the policy lands with high lateral velocity or angle (e.g., episode 2: vx=-0.099, vy=-0.103, angle=0.52; episode 3: vx=-0.087, vy=-0.031, angle=0.38; episode 4: vx=-0.023, vy=-0.006, angle=-0.57). The policy learns to reach the ground with both legs contacting (60% both_leg_contact_rate) but fails to stabilize on the pad (0% stable_touchdown_rate, 0% near_pad_rate). The crash_penalty (-50) is paid in 60% of episodes (unsafe terminal), making it the dominant signal. The shaping_reward (+1.25) and leg_contact_bonus (+2.0) provide weak positive signals. The fuel_penalty (-11.03) is now halved from -0.1 to -0.05, which reduced its dominance. The core issue is that the crash_penalty magnitude (-50) makes landing attempts that fail (due to high lateral velocity or angle) very costly, discouraging the policy from exploring the final touchdown phase aggressively enough to achieve stable landings on the pad.
reflection_diagnosis.component_interaction_diagnosis: crash_penalty (-50) dominates the episode-scale reward because 60% of episodes terminate with unsafe terminal (crash), paying -50 each time. The fuel_penalty (-11.03) is the second largest negative component but is now halved from -0.1 to -0.05, reducing its dominance. The orientation_penalty (-5.91) is the third largest negative. The leg_contact_bonus (+2.0) is positive but small. The shaping_reward (+1.25) is positive but small. The success_bonus (100) is never paid (mean 0.0). The vertical_speed_penalty is never triggered (mean 0.0) because the policy keeps vy < 0.5. The interaction is: the policy learns to descend to the ground with both legs contacting (60% both_leg_contact_rate) but fails to stabilize on the pad (0% stable_touchdown_rate, 0% near_pad_rate). The crash_penalty (-50) punishes these failed landing attempts heavily, making the total reward negative (-63.69 generated reward). The policy is caught in a local optimum where it reaches the ground but crashes due to high lateral velocity or angle, and the crash_penalty discourages further exploration of more precise landing. The success_bonus (100) is too sparse and its conditions (|angle|<0.1, |x|<0.1, y<0.2, |vx|<0.1, |vy|<0.1) are too strict for the current policy's landing quality.
reflection_diagnosis.action_coverage_diagnosis: All four discrete actions (0,1,2,3) are used with coverage ratio 1.0. Action 2 (main engine) is dominant at 46.5%, action 0 (do nothing) at 35.4%, action 3 (right orientation) at 10.9%, action 1 (left orientation) at 7.2%. No unused actions. The bottleneck is not action coverage but trajectory-phase completion: the policy reaches the ground with both legs contacting (60%) but fails to stabilize on the pad (0% stable_touchdown_rate, 0% near_pad_rate). The final states show the lander is far from the pad (|x| > 0.25 in all episodes) and has high angle (up to 0.57 rad) or high lateral velocity (up to -0.099). The policy needs better phase guidance for the final touchdown phase (Phase 3) to achieve stable landings on the pad.
reflection_diagnosis.failed_pattern_reuse_check: The negative edges from iter_001 to iter_002, iter_003, iter_004, and iter_005 are all closed branches. The common failure pattern across all children was the addition of some form of per-step timeout penalty (ranging from -0.02 to -0.1) combined with other changes (angle relaxation, conditional fuel_penalty, near_pad_bonus, success_bonus increase). The next edit must avoid adding any per-step timeout penalty, must avoid relaxing the success_bonus angle condition, must avoid adding a near_pad_bonus, must avoid increasing the success_bonus scale, and must avoid making the fuel_penalty conditional on altitude. The only change should be reducing the crash_penalty scale from -50 to -25, keeping all other components identical to iter_006. This directly addresses the new scale imbalance (crash_penalty dominance) without introducing any of the failed patterns. The positive reference from iter_005 to iter_006 (fuel_penalty halved from -0.1 to -0.05) is preserved in the current design (fuel_penalty is already -0.05).

edit_summary.target_behavior_plan: The revised reward reduces the crash_penalty scale from -50 to -25, halving the dominant penalty. This directly addresses the scale imbalance: the crash_penalty was 4.53x the next component and 16.94x the positive objective budget. With the reduced crash penalty, failed landing attempts (which currently occur in 60% of episodes) will be less costly, allowing the policy to explore more precise landings that can trigger the success_bonus (100). The success_bonus (100) remains unchanged and provides a strong terminal signal. The shaping_reward (progress-delta) continues to provide positive feedback for reducing distance and vertical speed. The leg_contact_bonus (10) remains one-shot. The fuel_penalty (-0.05) remains unchanged. The orientation_penalty (-0.1) remains unchanged. The vertical_speed_penalty (-1.0) remains unchanged. The expected outcome is that the policy will explore landing more aggressively, increasing success_like_terminal_rate from 0.4 to >=0.6 and decreasing unsafe_terminal_rate from 0.6 to <=0.3.
edit_summary.action_coverage_plan: Action coverage is already 100%. No changes needed. The revised reward should maintain or increase main engine usage for controlled descent and landing, while encouraging more precise use of orientation engines (actions 1 and 3) to stabilize the lander on the pad.
edit_summary.phase_guidance_plan: Phase 1 (high altitude): shaping_reward encourages descending toward pad, fuel_penalty (-0.05) discourages excessive main engine use. Phase 2 (low altitude): shaping_reward continues, fuel_penalty continues at reduced rate, vertical_speed_penalty discourages hard landings. Phase 3 (touchdown): leg_contact_bonus and success_bonus reward proper landing. The reduced crash penalty (-25 instead of -50) makes Phase 3 failures less costly, encouraging the policy to explore more precise landings that can trigger the success_bonus.
edit_summary.payment_mode_plan: success_bonus is sparse (one-shot at terminal success). leg_contact_bonus is event-gated (one-shot). shaping_reward is progress-delta (not repeatable in the same sense). fuel_penalty is dense per-step penalty but now halved. orientation_penalty is dense per-step penalty. vertical_speed_penalty is dense but conditional. crash_penalty is sparse at termination but now halved. All positive terms are either sparse, event-gated, or progress-delta. No repeatable positive terms without success.
